name: Tangier
hero_subtitle: Views over the Strait, a stepped medina, and the meeting of Atlantic and Mediterranean light.

info.vibe_val: Port city, Strait winds and historic lanes
info.airport_val: Ibn Battuta Airport TNG · Al Boraq to Rabat/Casablanca · Ferries from Spain

overview.title: Welcome to Tangier — Gateway between Europe and Africa
overview.p1: Tangier sits where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean, with a medina climbing toward the kasbah and a modern seafront strip. A transit city: ferries from Spain, Al Boraq train south, and roads toward Chefchaouen, Asilah and Tetouan.
overview.p2: Give yourself two or three days: medina and kasbah, Café Hafa on the cliffs, Cap Spartel and Hercules Caves to the west, and an easy seafront walk. Stay near the medina for atmosphere or on the corniche for beach access.

places.title: Places not to miss in Tangier
places.subtitle: Medina lanes, cliff cafés and Atlantic headlands.

medina.name: Tangier Medina
medina.desc: White streets, Petit Socco and gates toward the kasbah.

kasbah.name: Kasbah Museum
kasbah.desc: Palace-museum on the hill with views over the Strait and rooftops.

socco.name: Grand Socco
socco.desc: Main square between the new town and medina gates.

hafa.name: Café Hafa
hafa.desc: Mint tea on terraces above the Strait of Gibraltar.

beach.name: Tangier Beach
beach.desc: Long urban corniche for walking and sea breeze.

spartel.name: Cap Spartel
spartel.desc: Lighthouse and headland west of the city, often with Hercules Caves.

caves.name: Hercules Caves
caves.desc: Coastal caves and the famous opening to the ocean near Cap Spartel.

legation.name: American Legation
legation.desc: Museum and courtyard inside the medina.

itinerary.title: 3 Days in Tangier
itinerary.subtitle: A flexible framework — adjust it according to your arrival and day trips.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter from Grand Socco, wander the lanes and stop for coffee in Petit Socco.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Climb to the Kasbah for the museum and terraces overlooking the Strait.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Mint tea on the cliff terraces as the light fades over the water.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Taxi west to the lighthouse and the Atlantic horizon.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Short stop at the coastal caves and the famous opening to the ocean.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Return to the medina for a restaurant, or a quieter option in the new town.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Tangier Beach or Cap Malabata
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Quiet morning on the beach/corniche, or east to Cap Malabata for open views.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Afternoon — American Legation or Free Time
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Visit the American Legation in the medina, or free time for shopping and cafés.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Train or road toward Rabat, Chefchaouen or the airport according to your route.

stays.title: Where to stay in Tangier? Our favourites
stays.subtitle: Kasbah riads with Strait views, a historic hotel and a beach resort at Malabata.

card1.name: La Tangerina
card1.desc: Iconic kasbah riad with terraces over the medina and Strait of Gibraltar — classic Tangier.

card2.name: Nord Pinus Tanger
card2.desc: Bold design hotel in the kasbah, pool and panoramic views toward Spain.

card3.name: Hotel El Minzah
card3.desc: Historic palace hotel near Grand Socco — gardens, old-world charm and a central base for the medina.

card4.name: Mövenpick Malabata
card4.desc: Resort on Malabata Bay — pool, beach access and modern comfort away from medina bustle.

eat.title: Where to eat in Tangier
eat.subtitle: Family tables, traditional tajines, port fish and mint tea — no bar scene.

nomad.title: Le Saveur de Poisson
nomad.desc: Fish house with no menu — day’s catch, shared tables and a Tangier family classic.

jardin.title: Restaurant Hamadi
jardin.desc: Family Moroccan tables in the medina — tajines and couscous without a bar atmosphere.

fassia.title: Restaurant Al Andalous
fassia.desc: Simple family restaurant for couscous, grills and everyday Moroccan dishes.

moha.title: Restaurant As-Saada
moha.desc: Grills and tajines near Petit Socco — simple, affordable and family-friendly.

bacha.title: Port Fish
bacha.desc: Fresh grilled fish at the fishing port — simple plates, families and local prices.

elfenn.title: Café Hafa
elfenn.desc: Cliff terraces for mint tea and sunset over the Strait — not to miss with the family, not a nightlife spot.

booking_banner.title: Explore every stay in Tangier
booking_banner.desc: Compare live prices, read verified reviews and discover more riads, apartments and hotels on Booking.com.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Petit taxis for short hops; meter or agreed price. Walking works well in the medina and along the corniche.

bargain.title: Airport & train
bargain.desc: Ibn Battuta TNG airport serves the city. Al Boraq high-speed trains link Tangier with Rabat and Casablanca.

water.title: Day trips
water.desc: Chefchaouen, Asilah and Tetouan are the usual road outings; Cap Spartel is a half-day west of town.

daytrips.title: Day trips from Tangier
daytrips.subtitle: Blue medinas, Atlantic ramparts and Andalusian heritage within easy reach.

chefchaouen.name: Chefchaouen
chefchaouen.desc: Blue medina in the Rif — about 2–2.5 hours by road.

asilah.name: Asilah
asilah.desc: Atlantic medina and ramparts south of Tangier — about 1 hour.

tetouan.name: Tetouan
tetouan.desc: UNESCO medina and Andalusian heritage — about 1 hour east.

q1.question: How many days in Tangier?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the medina, kasbah, Café Hafa and Cap Spartel. A third day suits a beach morning or a trip to Asilah or Chefchaouen.

q2.question: Is Tangier only a transit city?
q2.answer: No — the medina, kasbah, Café Hafa and west-cape loop make it worth two or three nights on its own.

q3.question: How do I get to Tangier?
q3.answer: Tangier Ibn Battuta Airport (TNG), Al Boraq train from Rabat/Casablanca, and ferries from Spain.

q4.question: Best time to visit Tangier?
q4.answer: April–June and September–November for mild weather. Summer is warmer and busier; winter can be windy and wet.
